bullets.title: US-Canada Trade War Escalates: 50% Tariffs, Dollar-for-Dollar Retaliation
bullets.body: US-Canada trade talks collapsed Friday night, triggering 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods (steel, aluminum, plywood, lumber, autos) effective Saturday. Canadian PM Carney declared Canada 'at war,' pledged dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective Sept. 8 targeting steel, dairy, and electronics. CAD fell ~0.5% vs. USD; E-Mini S&P futures opened ~22bps below Friday close. USTR Greer says no new talks scheduled.

bullets.title: NVDA Earnings Wed Dominates the Tape; JPM Tactically Bullish, Options Imply 4.6% Move
bullets.body: NVDA reports Wednesday (consensus $91.8B revenue, +96.5% YoY; Data Center $85.3B; EPS $2.08). JPM tactically bullish but says a dual disappointment on NVDA + Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole speech could trigger a 3-4% SPX pullback. Options imply a 4.6% 1-day move. NVDA crowding >3SD long heading into print; retail dip-buying despite HF de-grossing. Jensen Huang visited Taiwan for 3rd time this year ahead of earnings.

bullets.title: NVDA Price Hikes 15-17% on AI Servers; Vera Rubin Rack at $8M
bullets.body: Nvidia notified its largest customers of AI server price increases exceeding 15-17%, driven by soaring memory costs, effective early 2027. Vera Rubin NVL72 racks reportedly priced at ~$8M (vs ~$4M for GB300). NVIDIA simultaneously struck a $6B licensing deal with Poolside to build open-weight models and is in talks to invest in Perplexity at a $30B+ valuation. Microsoft confirmed receipt of first production Vera Rubin GPUs at its data centers.

bullets.title: Hedge Funds De-Grossed AI/Tech at Fastest Pace Since Liberation Day; US L/S Leverage at 1-Year Low
bullets.body: GS TMT reports hedge funds net sold US equities at the fastest pace since Liberation Day, with US L/S net leverage falling to a 1-year low of 48.3%. Nine of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Industrials, and Utilities. GS TMT Momentum Pair fell 18% Tue-Fri last week. Both HFs and mutual funds selectively reduced AI holdings in Q2, though HF net exposure to US Semis rebounded to June extremes ahead of NVDA earnings. Retail investors were dip-buying NVDA, MU, and SNDK.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole Speech Friday; Fed Communication Vacuum Driving Yield Surge
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday at Jackson Hole (10 AM ET); market expects him to apply mild restraint via a higher Fed funds rate while reducing 10Y bond vol. 30Y Treasury yields hit 5.27%, the highest weekly close since June 2007. Fed rate hike probability in September futures rose to 39% from ~32%. Bessent's Treasury buyback expansion was framed as quasi-QE but failed to hold yields lower; Trump separately said Bessent 'acted alone.' Lack of Fed communication cited as amplifying yield surge. Core PCE remains above 3%.

bullets.title: Debasement Trade Back: Gold $4,700, Bitcoin +22% Weekly Surge, USD Below 99
bullets.body: Gold hit $4,700 (14-week high) and Bitcoin surged ~22% (a 7-sigma weekly move, breaking the 200-day MA), while the USD softened below 99 amid US fiscal concerns and Treasury buyback expansion. Gold call option demand hit a 6-month high. Pattern of Bitcoin's 2-year consolidation ending was framed as institutional/ETF adoption now dominant. The move was also described as a 'debasement trade' with BTC up 19% and gold up 6% on Bessent's buyback announcement.

bullets.title: Alibaba $10.2B Hong Kong Share Sale to Fund AI Capex; Stock Down 8-10%
bullets.body: Alibaba launched an HK$80B ($10.2B) share placement at HK$112.70/share (3.6% discount to reference price), its largest primary follow-on offering since listing, with 100% of proceeds earmarked for full-stack AI capabilities and infrastructure. HK shares fell 8-10% on the news. Cloud revenue is expected to accelerate >50% YoY in the September quarter. Alibaba's Qwen is the world's most popular LLM model family; management targets USD100B in external cloud revenue in five years.

bullets.title: AI Capex Arms Race Intensifying: Hyperscaler Debt Financing, $1T+ Expected Next Year
bullets.body: Multiple sources note hyperscaler capex estimates are being revised upward at historic rates, with $1T+ expected next year. Tech companies are turning to junk bond investors to fund AI infrastructure. AVGO is arranging ~$100B in financing ($60-70B senior + ~$30B junior) for AI infrastructure deployments (~2GW). NVDA is investing $1.5B with SB Energy/OpenAI to secure land, power, and shell infrastructure. UBS notes CLS supply-chain checks suggest market is materially underestimating AI infrastructure demand scale and duration.

bullets.title: AI Frontier Pricing Compresses: OpenAI Cuts GPT-5.6 Sol 20%+; Open-Weight Models Gaining
bullets.body: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol API pricing by more than 20% due to competitive pressure from open-weight models. DeepSeek V4 Pro is priced at $3.96/1M output tokens, undercutting frontier labs. Anthropic's Fable 5 is seeing disappointing demand, with spend plateauing at ~11% of overall company tool usage after two months. Open-source AI token share at Vercel jumped from 28% to 62% in two months, underscoring the commodity pricing shift in the inference market.

bullets.title: Power Shortage ~30 GW in C27, Data Centers as Political Flashpoint; Oct PSP Signing Deadline Critical
bullets.body: MS forecasts a ~30 GW power supply gap in C27 and ~53 GW in C28. Powered-shell lease rates have risen from ~$1.80/watt (Aug 2025) to $2.30-$2.40/watt. Morgan Stanley flags October 2026 as a critical PSP announcement window to begin DC construction before end-2027. Data centers have emerged as a key political flashpoint in midterm campaigns, with 71% of Americans opposing local DC construction (vs. 53% opposing nuclear). ERCOT 765 kV transmission uncertainty is a wildcard affecting site viability.

bullets.title: Broad Market: S&P -1.4% Last Week; September Seasonality Worst Month Historically
bullets.body: SPX fell 1.4% last week; NASDAQ off 2%+; semiconductors and memory were under outsized pressure. Broad market breadth remains supportive per Oppenheimer (equal-weight S&P, Russell, Dow making new highs) but momentum factor fell 7-9.5% last week, with 96th percentile concentration in AI idiosyncratic risk. Citi's CETS notes bond-equity correlation near 30-year highs, constraining risk-taking. September is historically the worst performing month; Q4 is typically the best. Flash PMIs imply ~3% real GDP Q3 growth.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz Risk Elevated; Strait Traffic Near-Zero Before Normalizing via Alternative Route
bullets.body: Strait of Hormuz traffic collapsed to ~1 ship transiting at one point over the weekend, before ~40 tankers used the southern Omani route on Friday. Iran threatened that no oil would leave Hormuz if neighboring countries cooperate with US economic measures; Iran also warned it could 'label neighbors as enemies.' Secretary Bessent described upcoming US Iran sanctions as an 'economic D-Day.' Treasury Secretary press conference was planned for Monday at 1 PM ET. Tanker spot rates are surging on geopolitical risk, with WTI sliding ~2% to $85/bbl Monday morning on position adjustments.

bullets.title: US National Debt Exceeds 100% of GDP; Japan Dumped $123B of Treasuries Since February
bullets.body: US federal debt held by the public surpassed 100% of GDP at ~$39.7 trillion. Japan sold ~$123B in Treasuries since February (including $26B in June), with holdings now at the lowest since January 2025. Ray Dalio warned a US debt crisis could be three years away, recommending up to 15% portfolio allocation to gold. Long-end yields broke above 5.3% for the first time since 2007 (UK 30Y at 5.83%, Japan at 4.10%). The 30Y mortgage rate hit 6.72%, the highest in over a year.

bullets.title: Key Earnings This Week: NVDA, MRVL, CRM, INTU, WSM
bullets.body: The critical week ahead includes NVDA (Wed, $92.16B revenue consensus), CRM (Wed, $11.33B), INTU (Tue, $4.27B), WSM (Wed before open, $1.93B), and MRVL (Thu, $2.72B, +35% YoY). Multiple banks note MRVL is expected to beat-and-raise on AI and networking strength, with data center revenue modeled up 35% Q/Q for July. AVGO FQ3 reports next week with $34B revenue guidance and $16B AI revenue expected.

bullets.title: Taiwan Indicts Nvidia and Super Micro Employees Over Alleged AI-Server Exports to China
bullets.body: Taiwan prosecutors indicted nine individuals including Nvidia and Super Micro employees over alleged illegal AI-server exports to China, concluded from a probe into high-end server exports. The case comes ahead of NVDA's Wednesday earnings report and amid ongoing US-China export controls that have China's AI chip self-sufficiency rising from 33% in 2024 to a projected 70% by 2030. YMTC separately targeting a CNY33B Shanghai IPO.

bullets.title: Quality/FCF Rotation Accelerating; MS Recommends Barbell Approach Spreading from AI Semis to Cyclicals
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes quality rotation is playing out, with high-FCF, high-gross-margin, asset-light stocks up 16% over the past two months. Services-oriented and fee-based sectors show the strongest earnings revisions. JPM recommends a barbell approach: spreading risk from AI/Memory/Semis to Mag7/Software and adding Financials, Energy, and Metals/Miners within Cyclicals. Precious metals remain attractive. Nomura notes Europe lurching right with markets showing little concern. EPS Momentum is outperforming Price Momentum (MS22EVPM index +12.9% since launch).

bullets.title: META $1T California Trial Overhang; RDDT Down 14% on ChatGPT Citation Share Collapse
bullets.body: Meta's federal teen safety trial began with state AGs seeking up to $1.4T in damages; Zuckerberg and Mosseri expected to testify over the 6-8 week trial. RDDT fell 14% despite S&P 500 entry as ChatGPT citation share fell from ~4% to <1%, threatening DAU trends and LLM licensing revenue. SPOT and NFLX outperformed as subscription-based safer havens; SPOT added $1.5B to buyback authorization.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi September Summit Seen as 'Managed Competition' Reinforcement; Nov 10 Policy Expirations Are Key Risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects the September 24 Trump-Xi summit to reinforce managed strategic competition without breakthrough. Three temporary trade measures expire simultaneously on November 10: Section 301 exclusion list, BIS Affiliates Rule suspension, and China's Wave 2 rare earth controls. Chinese rare earth exports to the US are already down 70% from January 2025 levels. US midterms are flagged as an underappreciated risk to the AI trade narrative.

bullets.title: Silicon Wafer Prices Up 10%, First Major Hike in 3+ Years; Memory Wall Worsening
bullets.body: Silicon wafer prices are rising 10% across all sizes (6", 8", 12"), the first major hike in over three years, as AI demand has absorbed excess supply. Micron CEO says he sees 'no end' to when memory supply will catch up with demand. Micron's compute is outrunning HBM bandwidth by 3x every two years per its own Hot Chips presentations. NAND makers are shifting to molybdenum word lines above 300 layers; W-to-Mo conversion expected to drive >$1B in new deposition tool sales in 2027.

bullets.title: BABA Raises $10.2B; Hyperscaler Capex Payback Shortens; China Cloud Accelerating
bullets.body: Alibaba's cloud revenue is expected to accelerate >50% YoY in the September quarter with strong ARR growth (RMB16bn in August, targeting USD4.5bn by year-end). Capex payback period of 3 years expected to shorten with in-house chips and GPM improvement. Jefferies expects BABA cloud to show further acceleration in Dec/Mar quarters. China and US CSPs both exceed 90% capex-to-OCF ratios. Alibaba's Qwen spinout as an independent subsidiary signals accelerating AI commercialization.
